cards.title: How should wordcount count words in text that is not ASCII?
cards.why: wc-3.2 waits on it; wc-3.1 (words) landed without it.
cards.context: awk splits words on ASCII blanks. Text with non-breaking spaces, or in scripts written without spaces, counts oddly. The fix is small either way; the choice is what users are promised.

choices.label: Split on every Unicode space
choices.consequence: What most people expect for European text. Scripts without spaces still count one word per run. One more test.

choices.label: Keep ASCII blanks, and document it
choices.consequence: No code change. The README says what counts as a word.

choices.label: Use a word segmenter library
choices.consequence: Right for every script, but the tool gains its first dependency.

answer.note: Yes, and say in the README that scripts without spaces are not segmented.
